newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sets dates for Chinese president's visit.
newsitem.headline: Russia sets dates for Chinese president's visit.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin will visit Russia from April 22 to 26 for talks with President Boris Yeltsin, the Kremlin said on Thursday.

The presidential press service said Jiang was expected to sign an accord with Yeltsin and the presidents of the Central Asian states of Tajikistan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan on reducing border forces.

Jiang will also discuss political and economic cooperation between Russia and China. Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen visited Moscow last month to prepare for Jiang's arrival although no date for the trip had yet been announced.

"The visit will be an important stage in the process of filling the new formula of Russia-China relations with real content -- an equal, trusted partnership aimed at strategic cooperation in the 21st century," a Kremlin statement said.

Russia is trying to build up relations gradually with China and has been looking to the East at a time when relations with Western governments are strained by differences over NATO's plans to expand eastwards.
Russia and China formed a strong alliance in the early 1950s but it degenerated into bitter rivalry for leadership of the communist world and led to border clashes in the late 1960s.
Relations have been gradually improving since the late 1980s but both China and Russia rule out the renewal of any military or political bloc.
Disputes over border demarcation were largely resolved in 1991 and Yeltsin had promised to finalise the issue this year.
Details of the planned border forces pact have not been released and China's ambassador to Moscow said last month they may be kept secret even after the agreement is signed.
China, Russia and the three Central Asian states signed an agreement last April committing themselves to a set of border confidence-building measures.
